content.introduction: American Airlines reported first-quarter 2026 financial results with record revenue of $13.9 billion, a GAAP net loss of $382 million, and an adjusted net loss of $267 million. The company anticipates modest profitability for the year.
body: # American Airlines Reports First-Quarter 2026 Financial Results. “American delivered record revenue in the first quarter, and we’re on track for another record in the second quarter,” said American’s CEO Robert Isom. “This revenue momentum is the result of focus on our four commercial priorities — elevating the customer experience, growing our global network, driving premium revenue and leading in loyalty. Even in a volatile operating environment, our pretax margin improved by nearly 2 points year over year, and we still anticipate modest profitability for the year assuming the current forward fuel curve. American had year-over-year total revenue growth of 10.8% in the quarter. Total unit revenue was 7.6% higher year over year, improving sequentially each month in the quarter, culminating with March domestic and international passenger unit revenue both up more than 10% year over year. Demand remains strong, and based on current bookings, American expects total revenue growth between 13.5% and 16.5% in the second quarter.

**American Airlines Group Inc. reported higher revenue but remained unprofitable in the first quarter of 2026.** Total operating revenues rose to $13.9 billion, up 10.8% from a year earlier, driven by stronger passenger demand and loyalty program activity. Passenger revenue increased to $12.5 billion, with revenue per seat mile up 6.5% as fares improved and planes flew slightly fuller. Operating loss narrowed to $41 million from $270 million, and net loss improved to $382 million from $473 million, as revenue gains outpaced higher costs for fuel and employee pay. The company generated $4.2 billion in operating cash, reduced total debt, refinanced key credit facilities, and ended the quarter with $6.4 billion of short-term investments and $3.5 billion of undrawn revolving credit capacity. **American Airlines Group** grew Q1 2026 revenue 10.8% to $13.9 billion, with passenger revenue up 9.7% and total revenue per available seat mile up 7.6%. Liquidity is supported by $6.4 billion of short-term investments and $3.5 billion of revolving and other facility capacity as of March 31, 2026.

* American Airlines posted record first-quarter 2026 revenue of $13.9 billion, up 10.8% from the prior year[1][2]. * GAAP net loss narrowed to $382 million, or $0.58 per diluted share, with adjusted net loss of $267 million[1][2]. * Total debt fell to $34.7 billion, the lowest since mid-2015, with $3.4 billion in free cash flow generated[1][2]. * Full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance held at ($0.40) to $1.10 despite over $4 billion in higher jet fuel costs[1][2]. American Airlines Group Inc. reported its highest first-quarter revenue on record at $13.9 billion for Q1 2026, a 10.8% increase year over year, though it recorded a GAAP net loss of $382 million due to higher jet fuel costs[1][2]. American Airlines generated $3.4 billion in free cash flow during the quarter, despite interest expenses of $397 million[1][2]. Full-year 2026 adjusted EPS is projected at ($0.40) to $1.10, flat from prior guidance, even with more than $4 billion in additional jet fuel expenses anticipated[1][2][3].
